evals.prompt: We have a roadmap for improving a model, but the first cheap representation probe was flat overall and improved only one target class. What should we try next?
evals.expected_output: Grounds the current objective and observation; Revises the eligible frontier from the asymmetric result; Recommends one evidence-linked next proof instead of continuing a fixed ladder; States positive, negative, and budget replan conditions; Keeps execution and campaign state with the owning workflow
assertions: Uses the new progress evidence to revise rather than replay the original roadmap order
Ranks the remaining frontier by bottleneck fit, information value, unlocks, cost, and risk
Selects one bounded first proof and names what would falsify it
States contingent replan conditions for the result
Does not execute the experiment, compile a Goal, or create a ticket per attempt

farplane.title: Leverage Advisor replans from asymmetric evidence
farplane.notes: Regression for roadmap plus progress selection.

evals.prompt: Help us choose the highest-potential next technique, but the project has no current technique list and the only notes are a vague two-year-old blog summary.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the evidence-thin candidate frontier; Routes a bounded parity or source-synthesis step; Requires source-backed candidate dispositions before ranking; Returns a source gap when research cannot run; Avoids fabricating a technique leaderboard
assertions: Recognizes that the current lever catalog is absent or stale
Routes bounded research or source synthesis rather than always researching
Requires adopt, adapt, reject, or defer dispositions before candidates enter the frontier
Returns a source gap when the missing evidence cannot be resolved
Does not invent precise expected lift or a SOTA ranking

farplane.title: Leverage Advisor exposes a source gap
farplane.notes: Protects conditional research and no-fabrication behavior.

evals.prompt: The next roadmap contains six small experiments under the same metric, evaluator, owner, and compute cap. Should I create six tasks?
evals.expected_output: Keeps one bounded campaign ticket; Treats experiments as progress entries and evidence receipts; Splits only for independent ownership, proof, approval, spend, or changed objective/evaluator boundaries; Names the accepted tradeoff; Avoids taking over ticket lifecycle
assertions: Recommends one campaign ticket while objective, evaluator, owner, and budget are stable
Treats individual experiments as ledger entries and artifacts rather than tickets
Names concrete conditions that would justify a child or new ticket
Preserves the domain executor and Goal Advisor ownership boundaries

farplane.title: Leverage Advisor preserves campaign ticket ownership
